question: Should OpenClaw pursue distributed job orchestration as a backend-neutral core/plugin API contract, document ScalyClaw/BullMQ-style orchestration as external only, or defer this broad layer to the narrower cron/session/runtime trackers?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend boundary, config shape, worker failure semantics, credential model, observability, and core-versus-plugin ownership require maintainer architecture intent.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
options.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, and observability before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.

options.title: Document External Pattern
options.body: Keep core single-process for now and document ScalyClaw/BullMQ-style orchestration as an external deployment or plugin pattern.

options.title: Defer To Narrower Trackers
options.body: Let cron HA, external session storage, and distributed runtime decisions settle first, then revisit whether a broader distributed worker layer is still needed.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Contract
recommendation.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, and observability before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.
